 BMW of North America is recalling nearly 721,000 thousand vehicles in the U.S. over a defect that could start a fire while the car is parked and turned off.
 According to a notice from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration , faulty water pumps in select BMW models could short circuit and spark disaster for vehicle owners.

 “An improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump may be exposed to water and short circuit, increasing the risk of a fire,” the agency said.

 The models included in the recall are below:
 2012-2016 BMW 3 Series
 2012-2016 BMW 5 Series
 2012–2015 BMW X1
 2012-2016 BMW Z4
 2013-2017 BMW X3
 2014-2016 BMW 2 Series coupe
 2014–2016 BMW 3 Series sportswagon
 2014-2016 BMW 328xi Gran Turismo
 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series convertible
 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series coupe
 2015-2016 BMW 2 Series convertible
 2015-2016 BMW 4 Series gran coupe
 2015-2018 BMW X4
 2016-2018 BMW X5 xDrive40e
 Affected vehicles underwent a similar recall in 2024. However, they all need further repair. To date, NHTSA said that BMW is aware of 10 incidents that may relate to the issue, but is not aware of any injuries or crashes. All the incidents, however, occurred in vehicles that were repaired under the previous recall two years ago.
 When will BMW repairs begin?
 The remedy to address the electrical connector on water pumps of recalled vehicles is currently undergoing development, the NHTSA wrote. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed out beginning next month on Dec. 25.
 Beginning on the same day, impacted vehicle identification numbers and license plates will also be searchable on the NHTSA recall page . Repairs will be provided by BMW at no cost.
 But for the time being, car owners are asked to park their vehicles outside and away from buildings. Drivers of any yearly models listed above are also advised to contact BMW directly at 800-525-7417 for more information.
 BMW did not immediately respond to Moneywise’s request for comment.

 The agency says that drivers can check if their vehicle is involved in a recall by using the NHTSA’s recalls lookup tool or by downloading its SaferCar app. If you do have an open recall, drivers should follow any “do not drive” or “park outside” warnings.
 Not every recall is safety related, but in the event yours is and there still isn’t a fix, you do have some options. If you can’t wait to use your car, contact your local dealership for a loaner car until a fix becomes available, according to Consumer Reports . You can also contact the manufacturer directly for a loaner vehicle. The manufacturer may also tell you how long it will take before a fix is available.
 If you strike out on both fronts, it may be time to ask your local dealership to buy back the vehicle from you or contact an attorney if you’re being strung out for months.
 “Sometimes you have to be the squeaky wheel,” Rosemary Shahan, president and founder advocacy group Consumers for Auto Reliability and Safety, told Consumer Reports in 2024. “They’re perfectly willing to string you along and tell you you need to be patient, but you’re not getting what you paid for. You paid for a safe, functioning car.”
